newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Taylor Woodrow caution on H2 div.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Taylor Woodrow caution on H2 div.

text.p: Taylor Woodrow Plc, the construction-to-housebuilding group, warned investors not to expect an automatic rise in the final dividend after receiving a 33 percent jump in the first half payout to 1p.
Colin Parsons, chairman, told Reuters: "Investors should not automatically expect a rise" despite the group's rosy start to the second half of the year.
"I am innately a cautious individual," said the chairman. "I don't want people counting their chickens before they hatch."
Parsons said the increase in the first half payout was "a little unexpected".

In the results statement itself, the group had explained that the large rise was part of its effort to rebalance payments between the two halves of the year. "This level of increase should not be taken as an indication of the increase, if any, in the final dividend."
Parson described the overall interim result as "a good wicket to bat on" in the second half, with improvements across all divisions. But he warned that construction in particular remained tough.
"The UK market is remarkably tight. There is very little profit in contracting," he said.
The division which cut its losses back sharply could move into "a marginal profit by the second half" said Parsons but he added it would have a negligible impact on group results.
Other units are seen moving ahead, with housing seen as the most dynamic business. The turnaround in the UK housing market is seen as sustainable. "It's the real thing," he said.
But despite improved performances in the UK and U.S., Canada and Australia in particular disappointed. Australia was described as "the poorest housing market for at least 10 years."
But despite the dismal conditions, Taylor Woodrow remained committed to the country, said Parson who added that he thought the market had now bottomed out and was poised for an upturn."
